selection_notes: Bounded, real-world Python 2 stdlib module (urllib.py, removed/split apart in Python 3's urllib.parse/urllib.request). Module-level free functions were chosen over class methods so each unit is independently classifiable/convertible without needing surrounding class state.

functions.name: unwrap
functions.why: Pure string slicing, no py2-only syntax or stdlib surface at all.

functions.name: splittype
functions.why: Regex-cache-via-global pattern; mechanical, no semantic drift risk.

functions.name: splitport
functions.why: Regex-based split, no py2-only constructs. Also exercised as a dependency of proxy_bypass_environment.

functions.name: splitattr
functions.why: No regex, pure list slicing. Trivial baseline case.

functions.name: unquote
functions.why: Branches on _is_unicode(s) vs plain str; py2's str/unicode split collapses into py3's single str type. A syntax-only conversion changes behavior for byte-string input, so this needs semantic understanding, not just a substitution rule.

functions.name: quote
functions.why: Flagship example for why behavioral diffing beats a syntax-only pass: `str(bytearray(xrange(256)))` builds a byte->str escaping table using py2's str/bytes-are-the-same-type assumption. A naive xrange->range fix still RUNS under Python 3 but silently builds the WRONG table. Only a sandboxed diff against real fixtures catches this; 'it parses and runs' does not.

functions.name: urlencode
functions.why: Uses the old-style `raise Type, msg, tb` three-argument raise syntax, a SyntaxError under Python 3 (not just a deprecation) that requires rewriting to `raise Type(msg).with_traceback(tb)`. Also has the same str/unicode branching as unquote.

functions.name: getproxies_environment
functions.why: No py2-only syntax, but the two-pass 'prefer lowercase env var' logic is a good template case that still needs a real fixture-based diff to catch an off-by-one-pass translation bug.

functions.name: proxy_bypass_environment
functions.why: Depends on splitport and getproxies_environment from this same slice, exercising intra-slice function dependencies rather than isolated leaf functions.

unsupported_note: No function in this slice was hand-picked as 'unsupported' (e.g. use of `exec` statements, old-style classes with __metaclass__, or calls into stdlib modules removed outright in Python 3 like htmllib/rfc822). The classifier should still be free to tag any of the above as unsupported if its static analysis disagrees with this manifest's expectation — this list documents intent for test-writing, not a hard override.
